data.checks#Checks: A check must have run, every check that ran must have passed, and GitHub must say the pull request is mergeable.
data.merge-gates#Merge gates: Every merge in the fleet goes through ghmerge (and ghrelease, which calls it). It merges on evidence, not on the absence of a failure.
data.the-issues-gate#The issues gate:
A pull request must not land while an issue it mentions is left silently open. Before any write, ghmerge reads the pull request body and resolves each #N or owner/repo#N with one REST call. Each open issue must be preceded, on the same line, by:
a closing keyword (Closes, Fixes, Resolves and their other forms): the issue is closed by this pull request; or Refs: the issue stays open on purpose. A bare mention is refused, naming the issue and both forms. --issues-waiver "" merges anyway and records the reason as a comment on the pull request; there is no default and an empty reason is refused.
After the merge, every issue closed by keyword is read back. If GitHub did not close it (another repository, a base branch that is not the default, a missing permission) ghmerge closes it with the comment Closed by # (merge ). If it cannot, it exits 3 naming the issue.
The full rules are in the gitsafe README.
